newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police searching for kidnapped businessman.
newsitem.headline: German police searching for kidnapped businessman.

text.p: German police were still searching for a multi-millionaire Frankfurt businessman on Sunday three days after his brother paid a four million mark ($2.62 million) ransom to kidnappers.

Police said they had few clues to the whereabouts of Jakub Fiszmann, a 40-year-old businessman who was violently kidnapped on October 1. Police lifted a local news blackout on Saturday in the hopes of obtaining tips from the public.

Authorities believe Fiszmann, a member of one of Germany's wealthiest but most publicity-shy families, is still alive and being held captive near Frankfurt. Police confirmed reports the family has total assets that exceed 400 million marks.
"We have a very small number of clues," a spokesman for the state crime office in Wiesbaden said on Sunday.
Police said Fiszmann was attacked and pushed into a van in front of his company's office in Frankfurt at around 10.30 p.m. on October 1.
The businessman, who runs a property and electronics company in Frankfurt, apparently tried to fight off his kidnappers.
Fiszmann, whose father Uszer Josef Fiszmann came from a prominent Jewish family in Poland, also owns the GUM International Grosshandel and Marketing GmbH.
His broken wristwatch and small amounts of blood were later found in a white van police say was used in the kidnapping.
Fiszmann's brother paid the four million mark ransom, as the kidnappers had demanded, on Thursday. But they did not release Fiszmann as promised, the authorities said.
The four million mark payment was dropped off along a motorway north of Frankfurt on Thursday. Police did not provide any further details about the ransom payment.
Police said that the last time they had received any signs that the millionaire businessman was still alive was on October 2 when his voice was heard in a telephone message.
Authorities suspect that the kidnappers may be part of the same group that unsuccessfully tried to extort money during the aborted kidnapping of Fiszmann's nephew in 1991.
The nephew, who was six years old at the time, was released three days after he was kidnapped. Local media reports have said that the family paid one million marks ransom after he was released.
State police director Juergen Noeckel said that there were certain details in a letter from the kidnappers in this case that could only be known to the 1991 kidnappers. ($1=1.5293 Mark)
